title: Bobby Hundreds and Heather
summary: Episode 63 begins as a loose ensemble show and becomes two records. Bobby Hundreds discusses The Hundreds' tenth year, Ben Hundreds, streetwear community, recognition, family boundaries, social-media withdrawal, and the Ben Baller chain. A bassist then explicitly adopts the alias Heather before discussing an affair, divorce, grief, music, and dating. The cast immediately leaks enough tour, band, nationality, and relationship clues to re-identify her, so the editorial layer honors the stated alias rather than completing the doxxing puzzle. The second half moves through an improvised Bloody Dream performance, Asian and Filipino stereotypes, fake pregnancy and jewelry fraud, private sexual stories, matchmaking an absent employee, trivia, and another nonconsensual bodily-contact penalty.
sensitivity: Explicit sexual content; protective alias and re-identification risk; affair and divorce; private former partners; grief and emotional distress; family and children; racial, disability, gender, and orientation slurs; reproductive coercion and fraud; urethral injury; employee matchmaking; threatened sexual force; bodily odor/contact.
speaker_policy: Named dialogue remains withheld. Episode 63 has zero diarized turns and only five coarse fixed-window embeddings for a large shifting ensemble. Segmentation was deliberately disabled, and no independently validated held-out identity test has passed. Public introductions support structure, not acoustic publication.
